# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_006_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 2, Chapter 2

**1** After she finished speaking she asked, "Would you like me to read to you?" "Please, my lady," I said. "Listen carefully," she replied. She opened the little book and read — not from the beginning, but from somewhere in the middle: **2** "Listen: O God of all Powers, who by your invisible and immeasurable might and your boundless wisdom created the world; who clothed your creation with beauty through your glorious design; who set the heavens in place by your powerful word and established the earth on the waters; who through your wisdom and foresight formed your holy church and blessed it — **3** he is clearing away the heavens and the mountains and the hills and the seas. Everything is being leveled for his chosen people, so that he can fulfill his glorious, joyful promise to them — as long as they keep the commandments they received in faith." **4** When the reading ended I got up and asked, "My lady, what does it mean when the heavens and mountains and hills and seas are removed?" She answered, "When all these things are taken away, they will each serve God's chosen in some way. Right now, the mountains, hills, seas, and heavens are enemies of the elect. Once they are removed, those who are faithful and wholehearted will inherit all the good things — but the wicked will be shut out." **5** She said, "I want you to understand something: I am all of these things at once — I am patience and love and truth; I am the foundation of the saints, their upbuilding, their protective wall, their tower, their power." "Lady, explain what you mean," I said. She replied, "Look — right in front of you. Can you see the great tower being built on the water, with its bright squared stones?"

---

*PNEUMA note: The Church self-identifies as all the virtues and architectural elements simultaneously — a remarkable theological statement about ecclesiology.*
